title: a-proofs-isolation-holds-however-it-is-invoked
intention: A proof's isolation holds however it is invoked: no proof run by a CC tool call or by codemother's verdict writes into live ~/.cairn.
why: Measured 2026-10-06: 88 of 290 proofs write live ~/.cairn when run outside the tester's seal (2705 paths), a CC session's hand run leaked 6 inference tickets, and codemother's verdict runs proofs bare at every PROVED. The lived symptom: the operator's live logs, trouble lanes and launcher pid files carry fixture writes nobody can tell from real ones. The seal is the single door; the hands that bypass it are refused or routed through it.
traces_to: Law 8 and Law 4: the seal is the one door, held by physics. the strace census harness (scratchpad census_pytest_writes.py, 2026-10-06: 88 of 290 proofs wrote 2705 paths into live ~/.cairn under raw pytest; one CC session's python3 run of e9a2's proof leaked 6 inference tickets).
how: Children: 1af0564c0db3 (bin: rewrite python3 proof runs under the seal and refuse pytest at PreToolUse), 2c9eeab2da87 (tester: publish a sealed exec), 68cef2ddd8ef (codemother verdict: run instruments through it). No conftest: nothing in the repo uses pytest (cairn/devices/tester/cli.py line 9), and CC's pytest hand is 1af0564c0db3's.

out: bin/cmd/proofgate: a convenience that rewrites the common spelling, no longer the seal (Q#101, open-49fc67a40ede)

measured.saw: CORRECTS the earlier entry naming sealed tester runs: the 11-16 00:57 MST fixture folders were written by BARE proof runs from a Dell-local CC session (3c92a7d8, worktree /home/akien/dev/src/wt-race): `timeout 200 env PYTHONPATH=. python3 <bus proof>` at 07:56:31, 07:57:17, 07:57:24, 07:57:58Z. The bus logged the caller as pid 2917713, `python3 cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_bounce_leaves_a_line_that_outlives_its_scratch_home.py`, test=None, scratch home tagged with the HOST pid namespace 4026531836; its namespace guard ran (readlink unit 00:57:25) and found it beside the manager. HOME=/home/akien in a bounce line is no evidence of escape: the seal keeps HOME and binds a swap over ~/.cairn.
measured.how: ~/.cairn/logs/bus.log stop line (caller_pid, caller_cmd); bounces.jsonl test field; journalctl --user units 00:56-00:58; Dell transcript 3c92a7d8 tool calls

measured.saw: the 11-12 19:4x MST fixture window matches bare runs by Dell-local session 546bccde at 2026-11-13T02:42:06Z and 02:49:07Z: `for p in <ticket and bus proofs>; do timeout 300 python3 $p; done` in scratch worktrees; the proof path rides a shell variable, which no text gate can read
measured.how: Dell transcript 546bccde tool calls in the window

measured.saw: today's proofgate.judge rewrites `cd <wt> && timeout 200 env PYTHONPATH=. python3 <proof> | head` to `cairn test --exec`; bin/cmd/proofgate has no commit since 2026-11-15, so why the 11-16 run went bare is unmeasured (hook not firing in that session is the hypothesis)
measured.how: proofgate.judge on the Dell over the transcript's spelling; git log -- bin/cmd/proofgate

measured.saw: inside `cairn test --exec`, remote._beside_the_manager() returns False (own mnt ns 4026533108, manager's 4026531832), so a sealed caller's scratch bus takes setsid; outside it returns True
measured.how: scratchpad beside_probe.py run bare and under cairn test --exec on akiendelllinux

measured.saw: the tester's bwrap (isolation.py:757, and instance_bind_flags) passes neither --die-with-parent nor --unshare-pid: a sealed `cairn test --exec` runs in the host pid namespace (pid:[4026531836]). Of two setsid children it started, the one carrying CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID was gone 4 s after the run returned, and the one with the id stripped (env -u) outlived the sandbox, still in the run's mount namespace (mnt 4026532367, ~/.cairn dev 40 vs live 2050), holding the swap mounted until ended by hand. The collector is bf3c16162827's kill_what_it_started (tester/runs.py:188, called at device.py:826 for --seal and :1023 for --exec): it TERMs, then KILLs, every /proc process whose environ carries the run's id. A setsid loop spawned by Popen inherits the environment, so it carries the id and is collected by pid with no change to the tester.
measured.how: akienasus, bin/cairn test --exec starting `setsid python3 -c sleep` with and without the id; ps, readlink /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt, stat /proc/<pid>/root/home/akien/.cairn after the run; grep of isolation.py and runs.py

measured.saw: inside `bin/cairn test --exec` on akiendelllinux: live ~/.cairn dev=66306 ino=29109833; sealed ~/.cairn dev=50; `systemd-run --user --wait --pipe stat ~/.cairn` from inside the seal reads dev=66306 ino=29109833 (the live tree); `setsid -w stat ~/.cairn` reads dev=50 (the swap). A systemd-run unit escapes the seal; a setsid child stays in it. CORRECTED 2026-11-18 (orchestrator, re-measured): right about systemd-run itself, wrong about the bus taking that path; remote._beside_the_manager() is False under the seal, so remote.py:233 already spawns with setsid; the unguarded systemd-run spawn is the ground loop, cairn/tools/base/shim.py:189.
measured.how: orchestrator, stat of ~/.cairn from a sealed exec, direct and through each spawn spelling

outcomes.claim: no proof run writes live ~/.cairn: running the bus proofs that make fixture devices (test_a_wake_never_waits_under_the_hold_lock, test_mail_in_delivery_is_never_bounced, test_a_gone_clients_request_is_not_run) under `bin/cairn test --seal`, and the same proof as a bare `python3 <proof>` (no tester seal), leaves the live ~/.cairn/devices listing (names + mtimes) byte-identical before and after; the bare run refuses before its first tooth

outcomes.text: D5: a proof refuses to run outside the tester's seal: the scratch door (cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py, which the fixture proofs already enter) raises a named refusal when CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID is absent and the process is not under a sealed swap (isolation.sealed). One check, no spelling enumerated (outline 9.4.2.5.1, Q#101 / open-49fc67a40ede answer (a)).
outcomes.claim: a proof that enters the scratch door outside the tester's seal is refused by name before its first tooth, and writes nothing into live ~/.cairn

outcomes.text: D6: a loop a sealed run spawns stays in the seal: cairn/tools/base/shim.py's ground-loop spawn (systemd-run at :189) takes the namespace guard the bus spawn already has (remote._beside_the_manager, remote.py:354), so under a swap it spawns with setsid, inheriting the run's environment and so its CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID. The tester's stop already collects it by pid (bf3c16162827, kill_what_it_started; measured 2026-11-18), so no tester change. Re-aim cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_loop_a_test_run_starts_is_the_runs.py to 2120e74dcf44's why, measured by pid and not by a manager record (orchestrator ruling 2026-11-18: the unit was the means, not the outcome): the loop a sealed run starts carries the run's test id, runs in the run's mount namespace, and is not running once the run ends; 45c168cc1ff1 clause 2 says the same. Bounds: cairn/tools/base/shim.py and that proof.
outcomes.claim: a ground loop a sealed run spawns is spawned with setsid and sees the run's swapped ~/.cairn, not the live one; outside the seal's marker the loop spawns as a user-manager unit as before

D7: the proof bin/proofs/test_a_proof_run_by_any_spelling_is_sealed.py measures outcome 1 under a scratch commons: listing of live ~/.cairn/devices before/after a sealed run and a bare run of one fixture bus proof; teeth: sealed run adds nothing; bare run refuses and adds nothing. A further tooth for D6: a sealed run spawns a scratch bus, and the bus process's view of ~/.cairn (stat via /proc/<pid>/root or the bus reporting os.stat) has st_dev equal to the run's own ~/.cairn st_dev and unequal to the live one.

D8: HYPOTHESIS (outline 0.6.1, CC's answer, not a question): On Windows there is no bwrap seal; the tester's scratch-HOME path (d95796cdfb9b: HOME/USERPROFILE point at a per-run scratch dir) is the seal there, so D5's check counts a run as sealed when CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID is set and Path.home() resolves under that run's scratch dir; with no systemd-run on Windows, D6 is a no-op there. WATCHME(windows_proof_runs_stay_off_live_cairn): trigger each `cairn test --seal` batch on a Windows box; enough 10 batches with 0 new or touched entries under the live %USERPROFILE%\.cairn\devices, or the first nonzero (kills the hypothesis); carrier a verdict against outcome 1 on Windows: before/after listing of live .cairn\devices; consumer cc_0.
